text: At Levante, Barcelona were three goals ahead. Comfortable? It should have been. Then a poor backpass helped the home side score in the seventy-ninth minute. In the eighty-eighth, Levante scored again. Three-nil had become three-two. Suddenly, a match that looked finished had a completely different feeling. Adeyemi eventually made it four-two in stoppage time, and Barcelona kept their perfect record. But the warning survives the result. An attack this productive can cover up moments that become much more expensive against stronger opposition. And we should be precise: that first concession was a backpass mistake. Calling every conceded goal a high-line problem would miss what actually happened. The bigger question is concentration and control. Can Barcelona manage a lead with the same clarity they use to build one? Against Europe's best, that may matter just as much as another spectacular finish.
